rows.title_full: AN ACT REGULATING THE MANUFACTURE, USE, SALE, PACKAGING, DISTRIBUTION AND ADVERTISEMENTS OF VAPOR PRODUCTS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Refers \"Vapor Products\" as battery-powered devices that heat a solution, blend or gel, which may or may not contain nicotine, to a temperature that allows the production of vapor, also termed as Electronic Nicotine or Electronic Non-Nicotine Delivery Systems ( E N D S / E N N D S ).

Aims to mitigate and monitor the risks of Vapor Products by imposing strict product standards and comprehensive restrictions on their sales and consumption through: creation of an Inter-Agency Committee; protection of minors; ban on flavorings, except for tobacco and menthol; maintenance of post - market records on adverse health events; prohibition against use in certain public
places; severe penalties for non - compliance, among others.

rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE PHILIPPINE MARSHAL SERVICE, DEFINING ITS FUNCTIONS AND POWERS, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Seeks to defend and secure justices, judges, court officials and personnel in order to adequately 
protect their safety and independence.

Provides that the officials and personnel of the Marshal Service shall: possess suitable and adequate
firearms; be given the power to make arrests, searches and seizures, and to issue subpoenas for the appearance of any person for investigation; ensure that court trials and hearings proceed orderly, and to assist in the execution and implementation of court orders; and shall also be responsible in conducting investigation concerning allegations of irregularities, including graft and corruption, committed by aforementioned court officials and personnel.

rows.author: J092
rows.title_full: AN ACT PUNISHING MILITARY COMMANDERS OR SUPERIORS FOR CRIMES OR OFFENSES COMMITTED BY THEIR SUBORDINATES UNDER THE PRINCIPLE OF COMMAND RESPONSIBILITY
rows.abstract:
Seeks to address the alleged state of human rights in the country today which is impunity, in relation to the administration's campaign against drugs which involves numerous cases of extrajudicial killings and enforced disappearance.

Defines Command Responsibility as the responsibility of a military commander or superior for a crime or offense committed by a subordinate under his or her effective command and control if the commander or superior knew or under the circumstances should have known that the subordinate committed, was committing or about to commit such crime or offense and he or she failed to take all the necessary and reasonable measures to prevent or repress such acts, or submit the matter to competent authorities for investigation and prosecution, as the case may be.

rows.author: F061
rows.title_full: AN ACT CODIFYING THE ALTERNATIVE CHILD CARE LAWS AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract:
Seeks to address the needs of abandoned and neglected Filipino children by codifying the laws and simplifying the processes involved in providing these children a second chance of having the family care and love they deserve through out-of-home care such as that provided by residential facilities.

Proposes to create the National Authority for Child Care (NACC), a one stop shop on alternative child care attached to the DSWD - reorganizing the Inter Country Adoption Board (ICAB); and makes adoption administrative in nature to effectively streamline adoption procedures and make formal adoption accessible.

Provides for other forms of alternative child care such as guardianship, khafallah, kinship care,
or residential care.
rows.status: Transmmitted to the Committee on Ways and Means on 2021-05-20

rows.author: E050
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 1146, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE \"GOVERNMENT INSURANCE ACT OF 1977\" AS AMENDED, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Aims to address the prolonged dependence of Filipino children to their parents, due to the passing of Republic Act No.10533 or better known as the K-12 Law which mandated Filipino children to stay in school for a longer period of time.

Seeks to extend the coverage of P.D.No.1146, as amended, by extending the age of legal dependents from eighteen (18) to twenty-three (23), hence complementing the age when Filipino students normally finish their basic education and thus able to provide for themselves.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT ENTERPRISES AND PRIVATIZATION since 2019-11-27

rows.author: E050
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8282, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE \"SOCIAL SECURITY LAW\" AS AMENDED, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Proposes to amend the SSS law so as to supplement the change brought about by the K-12 Law by extending the age of legal dependents from twenty-one (21) to twenty-three (23), hence complementing the age when Filipino students normally finish their basic education and thus are able to provide for themselves.

States that Sec.8 (e)(3)(2) of R.A.8282, as amended, shall be read as follows:
SEC. 8. Terms Defined - For the purposes of this Act, the fiollowing. terms shall, unless the context
indicates otherwise, have the following meanings:
	\"e) Dependents -The dependent shall be the following.:
		(2) The legitimate, legitimated, or legally adopted, and illegitimate child who
is unmarried, not gainfully employed and has not reached TWENTY-THREE (23) years of age, or if over TWENTY-THREE (23) years of age, he is congenitally or while still a minor has been permanently incapacitated and incapable of self-support, physically or mentally; and ...

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE PROTECTION OF WORKERS IN THE BUSINESS PROCESS OUTSOURCING (BPO) INDUSTRY
rows.abstract:
Refers \"Business Process Outsourcing\" or \"BPO\" as the transfer of an organization's
non-core processes to a third-party who uses an information technology-based service
delivery, and in turn manages the selected process based on defined and measurable
performance criteria.

Seeks to protect the interests and welfare of the workers in the BPO Industry by giving them
the right to social protection that includes among others, the right to privacy of personal
calls, and for the night shift workers/employees to  have the right to stay in a
comfortable resting area within the employer's premises until daybreak to ensure their
safety.
